reason: Re-read internal/acdsl/policy.go confirms the chain exactly as claimed: policyBase() (line 195-218) sets candidates=[]string{policy.BaseRef} whenever the WORKING policy's BaseRef is non-empty, skipping the safe origin/HEAD, origin/main, main, master fallback entirely; GitMergeBase runs `git merge-base HEAD <ref>`, so BaseRef="HEAD" resolves to HEAD's own SHA; CheckPolicy then calls basePolicy(ctx, root, base, policy), which reads acdsl/policy.json via `git show <base>:acdsl/policy.json` -- since base IS the current HEAD commit, this re-reads the exact same forged, attacker-committed policy.json. A built fixture (base commit mode=strict + registry.json={c}; a branch commit that both sets base_ref="HEAD" and adds an "evil" entry to acdsl/registry.json) run through the real prebuilt acdsl binary produces zero ACDSL-POLICY diagnostics, while the identical registry.json change on a branch without the self-referencing base_ref is correctly flagged (acdsl/registry.json:1: ... differs from the policy base). isBoundary (branch != baseName) stays true throughout, so this is not the base-branch exemption -- the self-management surface check is silently vacuous for any commit whose own policy.json points base_ref at itself. effect and exposure as filed (destructive: strict/gated mode can be defeated in one commit with zero diagnostics; rare: requires the attacker to also control a base_ref value, which is plausible but not the default path) both hold.

read: internal/acdsl/policy.go:195-219 (policyBase): candidates = []string{policy.BaseRef} when policy.BaseRef != "" -- no check that the ref is not self-referencing before it is trusted to pick the base commit.
internal/acdsl/policy.go:63-76 (basePolicy): reads acdsl/policy.json via GitShowFile(ctx, root, base, "acdsl/policy.json") -- whatever commit `base` names, including the working commit itself.
internal/acdsl/git.go:69-75 (GitMergeBase): runs `git merge-base HEAD <ref>` verbatim, so ref="HEAD" returns HEAD's own SHA.
cmd/acdsl/main.go:122-137 (runCheck): policy := acdsl.LoadPolicy(*root) (the working/HEAD policy.json) is exactly the `policy` argument CheckPolicy receives and policyBase reads BaseRef from.
evidence.probe_run: internal/acdsl/policy.go:195: policyBase() honors Policy.BaseRef="HEAD" from the branch's own working policy.json, so GitMergeBase resolves merge-base(HEAD,HEAD)=HEAD and CheckPolicy diffs acdsl/policy.json and acdsl/registry.json against that self-chosen commit -- a real registry.json change lands with zero ACDSL-POLICY diagnostics, while the identical change without the self-referencing base_ref is correctly flagged: [PROBE-CORRECTNESS-BLK-10-R2] correctness-blk-10-r2-selfref-bypass -- policyBase() lets Policy.BaseRef (an agent-editable field in acdsl/policy.json) be set to a self-referencing ref like HEAD ... ; acdsl: 1 violation(s) across 1 rule(s)
evidence.manual_control_run: Hand-built fixture under round-2/scratch/correctness-blk-10-r2/selfcheck: identical acdsl/registry.json surface change (adding an "evil" entry) committed on a branch WITHOUT base_ref override produced `acdsl/registry.json:1: policy(strict): acdsl/registry.json differs from the policy base ... [ACDSL-POLICY] ...; acdsl: 1 violation(s) across 0 rule(s)` (exit 2... actually exit 1) -- confirming the surface check works correctly absent the self-referencing base_ref, isolating the self-ref as the cause of the bypass.
